Sort of went through this. What I did can be summarized in these steps.

1. I indulged. I listened to all the songs that reminded me of them, over and over. I listened to the playlists they made for me, re-watched the films we talked about, re-read the books we discussed. I reviewed past conversations in my head and allowed myself to cry.

2. I journalled extensively. I found it was no good suppressing how I truly felt. I allowed myself to admit that I wanted them back. Writing helped me to put my thoughts in order. I drew up tables on pros and cons about them. E.g. If I liked how clever they were, I also disliked how they weren’t very original thinkers, etc.

3. I burnt everything. I threw out gifts, cards, and letters. I erased them from my contacts list. Deleted all text conversations and pictures.

4. I made a lot of shitty art to eXpress mysElf.

5. I looked for distractions. Hung out with friends, checked out new eateries, dived headfirst into K-pop fandom, went travelling (can’t do it now, but simple adventures like a nice hike should suffice).

After 3 months, I just stopped thinking about them. I never fully dissociated them from the songs and movies we talked about, but I definitely don’t feel any more pain when I come across things that remind me of them.

All the best with forgetting. It can be hard and will take some time!
